name: Prisoner Good Morning
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hands laced behind your head (prisoner position).
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back with a soft knee bend and flat back.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, torso near parallel.
Drive the hips forward to stand, squeezing the glutes.
longevityNotes: A strong hinge is back insurance. Learn it light, groove it often, and add load slowly — the goal is a back that never complains about picking things up.
overview: Prisoner Good Morning is a beginner hip-hinge exercise targeting the hamstrings, performed with just your bodyweight. The hinge is the foundation of safe lifting — it teaches you to load the hips, not the spine.
